outcome.technical: PRODUCT (plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py): _changed_between and _unheld no longer hand git-printed paths back to git as :(literal) pathspecs on the command line; each lists the whole tree once and narrows in Python through the new _literal_matches(names, paths), which keeps git's literal-pathspec semantics (the same path, or one below it as a directory, '/'-bounded). Reason: a Windows command line is UTF-16 and Git for Windows turns it into UTF-8, so a path whose bytes are not UTF-8 (decoded by _git_path to a surrogate escape) reaches git as the three bytes of an encoded surrogate, the pathspec matches nothing, and the path reads as held/unchanged - fail-open in the carry check (_unheld) and in recut_wrong/carry_beside_work (_changed_between). The 100-path argv batching in _unheld is gone with the argv. _git_path's docstring now states what the decode does and why such a path is never handed back as a pathspec. CASES (tests/test_drive_phase.py): ar20, ar20b and ar21 asserted the base file src/f3.txt against the LF literal _AR_IDLE_BASE, while _repo writes it in text mode, so the base holds CRLF on Windows (the sweep sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, so core.autocrlf is unset and git stores those bytes as they are). The product was right in all three: ar20 refused by name (the file's CRLF only failed the literal); ar20b put back an LF copy over a CRLF base, which is a real change outside the task's files, so the drive correctly went on to undeclared-change; ar21 closed with the base's CRLF file. Each case now reads the file's bytes off the tree before acting and compares with those (ar20b puts back exactly those bytes); _AR_IDLE_BASE is removed, with a comment on _AR_IDLE saying why; each label now prints the compared values. ar22 is rewritten: a fake carry_git (_command_line_git) answers listings and matches :(literal) pathspecs against the bytes a command line carries, run under _COMMAND_LINES = posix (utf-8/surrogateescape) and windows (utf-8/surrogatepass), over the listing [caf\xe9.txt, dir/inner.txt, dirt.txt, other.txt]; it asserts the listing comes back whole, _changed_between(paths=[caf, dir]) == [caf, dir/inner.txt] and _unheld(paths=[caf, other.txt]) == [caf, other.txt], so it fails if the narrowing drops the path, narrows nothing, ignores directories, or uses a bare prefix. EVIDENCE: (1) the ar22 body on the pre-fix product: 'posix PASS', 'windows FAIL between=[dir/inner.txt] unheld=[other.txt]' (the Windows bug, reproduced on macOS); after the fix both PASS. In-memory mutants of _literal_matches (no file edited): return-all, exact-only and bare-prefix each FAIL under both command lines. (2) Windows text mode emulated on macOS (scratch runner rebinding the suite's open() to write \r\n where no newline is given) over the ar block: HEAD's test file -> 'SELFTEST FAILED: 35/39', FAIL ar20, ar20b (the same undeclared-change src/f3.txt output as CI), ar21, plus ar22 (HEAD's version asserts the retired pathspec); this task's test file -> 'ALL PASS: 39/39'. (3) `python3 tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage ar-block` plain: exit 0, 39/39, 184 s on this Mac (measured once). (4) Gate: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py` exit 0, 'ok tests/test_drive_phase.py 653 cases [1672.3s, 117 blocks]'. (5) ruff check (both files) exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0; _deps.git_path_base_violations() == [] (the rows for _changed_between and _unheld are not stale: both still make a diff listing call); _output_lints house_style_violations, prose_number_claims, path_preamble_violations, depth_sensitive_paths: no hits. CP1252 1 TIMEOUT: the ar block holds 39 cases, each building a wave fixture with task worktrees and driving the drive several times, so it is dominated by git and Python process starts, which cost far more on Windows; it takes 184 s in one process on macOS. Its timeout comes from the file's recorded cost: sweep-selftests.file_timeout = TIMEOUT_PER_COST (3) x the recorded slot-seconds spread over the grant's slots, cut by the deadline, and .github/sweep-costs.json records 1346.4 for tests/test_drive_phase.py on windows-latest. That job's own row reports [4913.5s, 117 blocks] (windows plain 1: 4375.4s), so the file now costs about 3.2-3.6x its recorded figure (P142's cases), every block's timeout is sized off a stale figure, and cp1252's slower run pushed the ar block past 447 s. sweep-costs.json needs re-recording (`python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <windows log> --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`, or --record-costs); it is outside this task's files and was not touched. LEFT, NOT CHANGED: (a) _seed_from_index writes not-checked-out skip-worktree paths to update-index's stdin as os.fsencode(p); on Windows a path _git_path decoded through its escape fallback is re-encoded there as other bytes, and update-index fails, so carry_commit refuses out loud (not a silent pass). A true inverse needs a decode that is one-to-one on Windows, which would trade away opening files whose NTFS names carry unpaired surrogates; that is out of a minimal change. (b) tools/lints/_deps.py GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT reason rows for drive-phase.py tree_changed (line ~1950) and _changed_between (~1971) still say the paths are 'handed back as literal pathspecs' - their prose is now stale, though the lint passes; that file is outside this task's files. (c) Other :(literal) sites: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:609 and drive-phase.py aside_patch/set_aside build pathspecs from plan entries (text), not from git-printed bytes, so they are outside this class. COST FACT: _unheld now makes three whole-tree listings instead of up to three per batch of 100 paths; its ls-files -o walks the untracked, non-ignored part of the tree once more (git status --untracked-files=all already walks it in the same carry_commit). outcome.descriptive: The drive no longer passes git-printed paths back to git on the command line, where Windows cannot spell bytes that are not UTF-8, so the redo/carry checks hold on Windows; ar20/ar20b/ar21 now compare against the base's real bytes instead of an LF literal Windows' text-mode fixture never wrote.
